source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Retake the NCLEX at every routine renewal because re-examination is a universal renewal requirement.","B":"Verify the current renewal requirements of the licensing jurisdiction because continuing-competency, education, and other requirements vary by jurisdiction.","C":"Use the renewal requirements from the state of original licensure even when the active license is issued by another jurisdiction.","D":"Assume the license remains active indefinitely unless the employer requests a renewal."}}
source_row.rationale: Licensure renewal is governed by the applicable board of nursing. NCSBN recognizes renewal as a licensure process across jurisdictions, but specific renewal requirements vary; the nurse should verify the current requirements of the licensing jurisdiction rather than assume a universal CE rule.
source_row.source_detail: Licensure and renewal are governed by the applicable nursing regulatory body; requirements are jurisdiction-specific. Live NCSBN guidance currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A nurse is preparing to renew a nursing license. Which approach is most appropriate?
